summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list, replacing the old search form.

findings.title: URL query rendered as raw HTML
findings.problem: The heading injects query from the URL into raw HTML without escaping. An attacker controls q through a crafted link.
findings.consequence: A link such as ?q= runs attacker script in the victim's session. This is a reflected XSS.
findings.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect refetches on every render forever
findings.problem: The effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render. Each run calls setResults with a new array, which triggers another render.
findings.consequence: The page hits the catalog API in an endless loop. This wastes client and server resources for every visitor.
findings.fix: Pass [query] as the effect's dependency array.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.problem: SearchPage returns early when query is empty, before it calls useState and useEffect. The number of hooks therefore depends on q.
findings.consequence: React throws a hooks-order error when q changes between empty and non-empty on the same mounted page. The page then crashes.
findings.fix: Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Skip the fetch inside the effect when query is empty.

findings.title: Search input removed from the page
findings.problem: The change deletes the search form, yet the empty state tells users to type a search term. The page no longer has an input.
findings.consequence: Users who open /search without q cannot start a search. They must edit the URL by hand.
findings.fix: Keep the form with the q input and submit button, and render it alongside the empty state and the results.

findings.title: Search failure rejection is unhandled
findings.problem: searchProducts throws when the response is not ok, but the promise chain has no catch. The rejection floats.
findings.consequence: A failed search raises an unhandled rejection. The user sees an empty list with no error message.
findings.fix: Add a catch that records an error state and render a message for it.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: SearchPage gained an empty state, a fetch and result rendering. The repository has no test that exercises any of them.
findings.consequence: Regressions such as the render loop or the hooks-order crash can ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add component tests for the empty query, the results list and a failed search.

dropped.reason: Each list item is a stateless text node, so a missing key only causes a console warning. Reordering cannot lose any state here.
